meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax differentiation applicable to SAS incorporation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified continental commercial law tradition with constitutional and administrative-law overlay; FATF-aligned AML/CFT framework)

Tax treaties (DTAAs) in force with Spain, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Switzerland, Portugal, Italy, Mexico, Chile, Peru, Ecuador and South Korea

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation and suspicious-transaction reporting); Ley 1121 de 2006 (FATF 40 recommendations alignment); Ley 2010 de 2019 inserting Article 631-E of the Estatuto Tributario (beneficial-owner reporting duty); Resolución DIAN 164 de 2020 (UBO identification and reporting framework); Ley 2195 de 2022 (anti-corruption and beneficial-ownership transparency); Circular Externa 100-000022 de 2021 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (SAGRILAFT/UBO compliance for SAS entities); Código de Comercio arts. 98-178 on corporate formation and statutory representation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for member states) or Consular Legalization (for non-member jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate board of directors / notary public in country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by the Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s) to the Colombian incorporator or appointed representative

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories must be screened pre-incorporation and continuously thereafter against the OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated list, Colombian UIAF lists of PEPs and assets subject to freezing, and the Superintendencia de Sociedades SAGRILAFT risk categorization. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence and requires senior-management approval, with a two-year post-employment cooling-off period; re-screening is recommended at least every fifteen days and before each high-value transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) processed through the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá or the domiciliary chamber portal; online homonym and name-availability search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS corporate name must be submitted in Spanish or roman (Latin) characters; foreign words are permitted only in phonological transliteration acceptable to the registry; the distinguishing element must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already reserved in any Colombian chamber district, per Código de Comercio company-name rules and the chamber's Circular Básica Jurídica criteria.

Seguros / Aseguradora / Corredora de Seguros (prior SFC insurance authorization)
Fondo de Inversión / Fondo de Pensiones / Capitalización (prior SFC authorization)
Bolsa / Bursátil / Mercado Público de Valores (prior SFC authorization)
Cooperativa / Precooperativa (prior Superintendencia de Economía Solidaria approval)
Universidad / Colegio / Escuela / Centro de Formación (prior Ministry of Education approval)
Salud / EPS / IPS / Clínica / Hospital (prior Superintendencia Nacional de Salud approval)
Minero / Minería / Carbón / Litio / Exploración / Explotación (prior Ministry of Mines and Energy approval for the activity)
Petróleo / Petrolera / Oleoducto / Gas / Hidrocarburos (prior Ministry of Mines and Energy authorization)

Lotería / Apuestas / Casinos (prior regulatory authorization under coljuegos rules)

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the incorporator may (i) file a reposición (reconsideration) petition with the issuing Cámara de Comercio within the statutory CPACA window (generally ten (10) working days after notification), under Ley 1437 de 2011; (ii) if denied, file an apelación (appeal) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the corresponding CPACA term; (iii) in parallel, reserve an alternative name on RUES without duplicative payment of the homonym fee where the chamber fee schedule waives it for first replacement searches.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the battery-metals cross-border procurement model, provided the registered domicile (domicilio principal y notificación judicial) is a specific physical location in Colombia, can physically receive notifications, is consistent with the RUT address registered at DIAN, and the entity maintains electronic books available for inspection; a mailbox-only address is not acceptable before the Cámara de Comercio.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for commodity-trading SAS profiles: approximately 45% risk of an unannounced DIAN or Superintendencia de Sociedades inspection within the first 24 months, driven by invoice-import mismatch triggers, UBO reporting gaps, and export/import volume inconsistencies; the risk declines to roughly 15-20% where full bookkeeping, a resident agent, and complete SAGRILAFT files are maintained.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada regime), Articles 3, 5, 17, 22 and 27; Código de Comercio (Decree 410 of 1971), Articles 110, 354 and 372; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Unified Regulatory Decree for Commerce), Section 2.2.8; Superintendencia de Sociedades, Circular Básica Jurídica.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES), under the administrative oversight of the Superintendencia de Sociedades; tax identification (NIT/RUT) coordinated with DIAN.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento privado de constitución (private incorporation deed) executed by all shareholders, with signatures authenticated before a notary (or elevated to public deed only when real property is contributed), submitted for registration in the Registro Mercantil via the Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; Article 5 of Law 1258/2008 permits payment of the subscribed capital, in whole or in part, up to two years from incorporation. No escrow or blocked bank account is required; the deed must state the subscribed capital, paid capital, class and number of shares, and the payment schedule. For an illustrative subscribed capital of COP 200,000,000, the departmental registration tax (0.7% of subscribed capital) plus Chamber tariff results in total official filing fees of approximately USD 430.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] S.A.S.

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under Law 1258 of 2008 by private deed recorded with the Chamber of Commerce; and

WHEREAS, the Board must establish corporate governance and internal administration;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board resolves:

1. The issuance and subscription of one hundred (100) ordinary shares is ratified.
2. The registered office is adopted at the address stated in the articles of incorporation.
3. The legal representative and alternate representative are appointed with broad powers.
4. The legal representative is authorized to complete regulatory filings, open bank accounts, and execute operational contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (online RUES platform of the selected Chamber, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, through the Chamber's virtual channel, an application for the 'Certificado de homonimia' (name availability search) listing three corporate names in order of preference. The Chamber verifies that no identical or confusingly similar business name exists. Approval is issued electronically; the approved name is reserved and must be incorporated in the deed within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Application form for homonymy search (Formulario de consulta de homonimia)
Valid ID or passport copy of the applicant/shareholder
Three corporate name alternatives in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for identity or similarity with an existing registration, select the next alternative name and refile in the same virtual session; no penalty applies if refiled within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - online portal (MUIS) or integrated service point at the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) application with the company's proposed details, CIIU code 4662 (wholesale of ores and metals), economic activity description (cross-border procurement and trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate). Obtain the 'Pre-RUT' containing the provisional tax identification data required to complete mercantile registration.
required_dossiers: ID and domicile proof of the legal representative
Tax identification and apostilled legalization of foreign shareholders (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: DIAN may reject the pre-RUT for misclassification of activities; correct the economic activity and business description (aligning with CIIU 4662) and resubmit through the same digital application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarial Authentication of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and, for authentication, any Notary (Notaría) in Colombia; consular or apostilled signature mechanism for shareholders abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private incorporation deed covering statutory clauses: company name, domicile, duration (indefinite), corporate purpose, subscribed/paid capital, share classes and voting rights, board structure, representation and audit rules, and dispute resolution. All shareholders must sign; signatures are authenticated before a notary or equivalent authority abroad subject to apostille. Where real property is contributed, the deed must be executed as a public deed before a notary.
required_dossiers: Minuta/articles of incorporation signed by all shareholders
Valid national ID or passport of each shareholder
Apostilled and legalized notarized power of attorney (for remote or foreign shareholders)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary or reviewing authority may require formal corrections; rectify the identified clauses, re-execute the signatures, and re-present for authentication without restarting the process.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); electronic portal MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) at www.dian.gov.co; company incorporation and RUT pre-issuance coordinated through the Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) under the RUES system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Colombian S.A.S. must: (1) incorporate via private deed or public instrument and register the company before the competent Chamber of Commerce to obtain the existence and representation certificate; (2) file the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) with DIAN through MUISCA using the digital signature (firma electrónica) of the legal representative, thereby obtaining the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria); (3) activate the 'responsable del IVA' status and mandatory electronic invoicing authorization in the same RUT update. Non-resident shareholders do not require a Colombian NIT for holding shares, but dividend payments to them are subject to 10% withholding. The S.A.S. must appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia and, for fiscal purposes, an authorized public accountant; a foreign entity acting directly as a non-resident supplier with no permanent establishment must likewise obtain an NIT and designate a tax representative before issuing invoices to Colombian recipients.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists in Colombia; the S.A.S. is an autonomous juridical person taxed under the ordinary corporate regime (35% CIT, worldwide income, foreign tax credit). Available statutory elections relevant to the lithium carbonate arbitrage trade: (1) election to claim export VAT refunds on a bi-monthly basis in Form 300; (2) election to adopt the SIMPLE combined regime (income tax and VAT integrated) where annual gross revenue does not exceed 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706,500,000 in 2024), generally unsuitable for wholesale battery metals arbitrage; (3) election to allocate profits to a foreign PE under applicable DTA rules (Andean Community Decision 578) or domestic territorial attributions; (4) hybrid mismatch and interest-stripping elections per Law 2277/2022 (including the 30% EBITDA interest cap) that permit taxpayers to characterize certain payments consistently between jurisdictions; (5) customs regime elections (free trade zone, temporary import, or transit) for structuring the import-re-export chain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: Anti-hybrid rules require the Colombian entity to self-disclose hybrid instruments and entities; no protective check-the-box election equivalent to US '8846' or OECD Model PEs is available, and reliance on a foreign tax characterization must be documented in the transfer pricing master file.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado / Value Added Tax) administered by DIAN; supplementary Impuesto Nacional al Consumo on specific services and ICA (municipal industry and commerce tax) depending on domicile; goods exported from Colombian customs territory are subject to 0% IVA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold in Colombia: all persons performing taxable acts or activities must register as 'responsables del IVA' from the first transaction (Art. 555-2 E.T.). The former simplified regime was abolished in 2018; only natural persons with annual income below 3,500 UVT (COP 164.7 million in 2024) are exempt from invoicing requirements, a privilege not available to a wholesale S.A.S. For the SIMPLE combined regime, the annual turnover ceiling is 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706,500,000 in 2024).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta) under Resolution 000165/2023: invoices must be pre-validated in real time through DIAN's MUISCA web services (XML schemas 4.x), bear a unique CUFE/CUNE digital code and QR, and be transmitted to DIAN before issuance to the buyer. 'Documento soporte' electronic documents are required for acquisitions from non-obligated suppliers. Exporters claiming VAT refunds (saldo a favor) face enhanced validation, including DIAN's automated 'radar' system and mandatory certification of invoicing software providers. Failure to transmit or use unauthorized software renders invoices invalid for cost, expense, and VAT refund substantiation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_customs_integration: For export zero-rating, the electronic invoice must be cross-linked to the validated export declaration (DEX) and the foreign exchange settlement certificate within DIAN's customs and FX databases; discrepancies trigger automatic refund holds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% IVA rate applies to goods physically exported from Colombian customs territory on the basis of a validated export declaration (Art. 481 E.T., Decree 1165/2019). The S.A.S. trader must prove: (a) sale and invoice to a foreign counterparty outside Colombia, (b) physical departure of the goods from Colombian customs jurisdiction (if goods never enter Colombia and are transferred directly from remote supplier to buyer, no Colombian IVA arises for lack of nexus and the transaction is documented as an offshore sale), (c) ownership transfer and payment by the foreign buyer, and (d) settlement of the export proceeds through the Colombian foreign exchange market (MCR) by the exporter or its marketing agent. The resulting credit balance in the bi-monthly Form 300 is generally refundable (solicitud de devolución) or compensable after DIAN's automated two-return review.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX / Export Customs Declaration (Declaración de Exportación, electronically validated by DIAN in MUISCA, including customs manifest and zone registration)
Bill of Lading (original negotiable transport document evidencing loading on board a vessel in a Colombian port destined to a foreign port; AWB for air freight)

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Liquidación de Operaciones de Cambio / posición coordinada emitida por el intermediario cambiario) evidencing repatriation of export proceeds through the Colombian forex market
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, weight certificate, and origin/certificate of analysis for battery-grade lithium carbonate (as required by customs or customer contracts)
Bi-monthly IVA return (Formulario 300) with the export lines at 0% and the refundable balance calculation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN reviews under Arts. 705-773 E.T.: 3-year statute for corrective returns, 5 years for omissions, 10 years for fraudulent returns. Specific penalties for export fraud: failure to repatriate or to prove FX settlement within 180 days converts the 0% rate to taxable at 19% with moratory interest (1.5x ordinary debtor rate) and a 20% inaccuracy penalty under Art. 647 E.T., escalated to 100%-200% for simulated or reckless conduct; illegal appropriation of VAT refunds may trigger criminal tax evasion charges (Criminal Code Art. 434-B, imprisonment 4-9 years and fines up to 200% of evaded tax); unjustified refunds are clawed back with full principal, IPC indexation, moratory interest, and a penalty equal to the refunded amount. DIAN's customs intelligence unit cross-matches DEX, B/L, customs manifest, and FX certificates to detect circular transshipments, incoterm misdeclarations (EXW vs FOB), and overpricing that fabricate export refunds; lithium carbonate traders should expect intensified documentary inspection and denial of refunds if the goods do not clear customs through Colombia.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (BdR or BanRep), acting together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for the authorization and surveillance of foreign-exchange intermediaries, and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for customs/trade-related foreign-exchange records and export/import declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed but broadly free foreign-exchange market (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales) under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, and the BdR regulatory circuit (Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83). Current-account transactions (goods imports/exports, services, remittances of dividends) are freely convertible and require only the registration of each operation through an authorized intermediary (Declaración de Cambio). Capital-account operations, including foreign direct investment (FDI) in a Colombian S.A.S., are freely allowed but must be registered with BdR via the local bank using the international investment declaration (Form 3 of the Declaración de Cambio) within the statutory window (generally before disposition or repatriation, and practically within 12 months of the injection). Profit remittance is legally permissible and subject to no exchange-control quota; however, the paying bank will require (1) an up-to-date FDI registration, (2) proof of tax filing status and withholding levy under Article 245 of the Tax Statute (dividend withholding is applied by the bank at the withholding rate established for the resident/non-resident shareholder category), and (3) a FX declaration executed at the date of remittance. Failure to register the inbound FDI before dividend distribution blocks the remittance. For a trading company, the COP is a fully deliverable current-account currency, but offshore NDF/convertibility gaps exist for capital-account purposes; therefore, all inward arbitration receipts and outward supplier payments should be cleared through regulated local banks rather than offshore EMIs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts from the re-export of battery-grade lithium carbonate (or any Colombian-origin goods) must be repatriated through the official foreign-exchange market within the BdR statutory recaudo term (generally 12 months from the export shipment date, extendable subject to BdR authorization). The full gross export value is subject to the surrender/channeling obligation: the exporter must either convert the proceeds into COP through an authorized intermediary or credit them to a locally-held foreign-currency account or to a previously authorized compensation account abroad, in all cases filing the Declaración de Cambio de Exportación (Form 2). Funds not used for permitted current-account payments (e.g., import settlements) must be converted to COP. Import payments for lithium carbonate procurement, by contrast, are settled pursuant to the applied INCOTERM within the payment term reflected in the import declaration; payments made in advance of physical arrival are permitted but the goods must be imported within the BdR-imposed six-month term, failing which the prepayment is recharacterized as a capital outflow requiring a separate declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bancolombia S.A. (through its international trading/cash-management unit, BanColombia / Banca de Inversión)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Cuenta Corriente / Current account for operational FX and trade settlement; supports the FX Declaración de Cambio and Letter-of-Credit issuance
Operational current account with trade-finance desk (LC, collections, Carta de Crédito) and FX register support
Current account for liquidity clearing and import payment routing
Current account and FX derivative ISDA/back-to-back line for hedging lithium carbonate price and COP/USD exposures
Current account and customer account for USD clearing via Scotiabank network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary account. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Intergiro) cannot lawfully perform the mandatory Declaración de Cambio filings with BdR, cannot issue Colombian import-payment FX declarations, and are not authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries. Their use is limited to (i) holding of funds in accounts abroad where the Colombian entity has obtained a compensation-account authorization from BdR, or (ii) receiving commission rebates/ancillary payments; even then, the funds must eventually be channeled into Colombia via the official FX market. EMIs should be used only as ancillary liquidity in transit accounts and never as the settlement rail for trade payables.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for the legal representative and, in many banks, the principal shareholders/UBOs of a newly formed S.A.S. The Superintendencia Financiera's KYC rules (Circular Básica Jurídica, Part 1, Title IV) require face-to-face verification of identity documents and the signature of the bank's account contract and AML procedures; registration of the legal representative's power of attorney (if any) must be notarized and recorded with the Cámara de Comercio. Remote opening is generally not available for a trading company with foreign ownership; a hybrid on-site appearance at the branch in Bogotá/Medellín plus a notarized UBO declaration and apostilled board/shareholder resolutions for any foreign signatories is the practical minimum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed S.A.S. with no operating history and a foreign beneficial owner, concentrating on high-value commodity (battery-grade lithium carbonate) trade — typology of 'front-company trade' and round-tripping of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificado de existencia y representación legal emitted by Cámara de Comercio within 30 days; (2) RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and NIT certificate; (3) notarized incorporation bylaws and shareholders' resolution appointing the legal representative; (4) notarized UBO declaration identifying all natural persons above 10% ownership (or the statutory control threshold) with passports and proof of address; (5) source-of-funds statement for each capital contribution, supported by bank statements of the foreign shareholder and, if applicable, previous tax returns; (6) signed AML questionnaire and internal corporate AML manual; (7) trade documentation evidencing real transactions — proforma invoice from the lithium carbonate supplier, sales contracts/MOUs, cargo booking and transport documents, certificate of origin, and commodity quality certificate (Li2CO3 battery-grade specification); (8) letters of reference from the shareholder's existing bank(s) (SWIFT reference letters or bank comfort letters); (9) projected cash-flow and transaction-flow model demonstrating that wire volumes are consistent with the registered trade cycle; (10) rent/lease certificate and utility bills attesting to a physical office presence; (11) sworn declaration of non-involvement in PEP/OFAC/EU/UN sanctions, signed by UBOs; and (12) issuance of annual audited financial statements (or at least statutory financial statements) to evidence that flows are balanced and taxes are filed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI wire from a high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., China, Hong Kong, or UAE) to a newly opened account, followed by rapid outbound payment to the same or a related supplier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) The BdR international investment declaration (Form 3) evidencing the capital injection classification; (2) wire confirmation (SWIFT MT103) identifying the remitter as the registered shareholder; (3) an equity subscription agreement and the notarized minutes of the shareholders' meeting approving the capital increase; (4) the supplier contract and import proforma invoice matching the onward payment in goods and value; (5) customs registration of the import (for amounts above the DIAN threshold); and (6) transaction-flow narrative in the form of a 'trade rationale file' covering the purchase, freight, insurance, and final-trade margin, to demonstrate economic substance and avoid the 'pass-through fintech' red flag.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple large COP/USD conversions in a short period, indicating potential FX speculation or dividend-stripping, flagged by the bank's transaction-monitoring system.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) The import/export declarations (Form 1 / Form 2) matching each FX operation to an underlying trade; (2) a documented treasury hedging policy (forwards only, no naked FX positions); (3) board minutes approving the treasury mandate; and (4) monthly reconciliation of FX operations against outstanding trade contracts, attested by the statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal if appointed).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual mercantile registration renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late surcharge per month or fraction of month on the renewal fee after March 31; fines up to COP 1,000,000; registration lapse after prolonged non-renewal and risk of administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filed annual financial statements (Estados Financieros a diciembre 31) for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (commercial registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; approval mandatory by March 31, so filing is due by April 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to COP 2,000,000 per Chamber of Commerce regulations; suspension of annual compliance certificate; designation as an irregular company and potential administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting and approval of corporate accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record in Minute Book (no external filing unless acts affecting commercial registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held on or before March 31 of each year for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Superintendencia de Sociedades may order the meeting to be called; statutory auditor may report non-compliance; restrictions on dividend distribution and potential shareholder judicial actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of Final Beneficiary Registry (Actualización del Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 July, or the exact date fixed by DIAN's NIT-digit calendar published each December; the update window is normally in July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 5,000 UVT per omission (approx. USD 62,000 for 2025); late filing fines of 2,000 UVT per month; blocking of DIAN administrative procedures until regularized.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) required when the company's total gross assets or gross income exceed 3,000 times the Colombian minimum monthly legal wage (SMLMV) at the prior year-end; also mandatory for public issuers, financial entities, or companies expressly subject to Superintendencia de Sociedades supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian financial reporting standards under Law 1314 of 2009; typical SAS applies IFRS for SMEs (Group 2); a company crossing the Group 1 threshold of 30,000 SMLMV in assets or income, or classified as public interest entity, must apply full IFRS (NIIF).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must annually identify and confirm all ultimate beneficial owners (any natural person holding more than 5% capital share, voting rights, or effective control) in the DIAN RUBF. Any equity transfer or control change must be updated within 30 calendar days; the confirmation must include full names, IDs, fiscal residence, and percentage of economic rights.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,500 per year for registered office and resident agent services in main Colombian cities (Bogotá, Medellín, Cali); lower-cost virtual offices available at USD 300 - 600.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory for a typical procurement SAS below the 3,000 SMLMV audit threshold; voluntary certified audit ranges between USD 2,500 and USD 7,500 depending on transaction volume and complexity.
